notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped.

The breadboard uses the catalogue naming: bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. In the image the half with rows f-j is at the top and the half with rows a-e is at the bottom, so those rows map to banks 'b' and 't' respectively.

The image draws the bottom rails as an upper black (negative) row and a lower red (positive) row. They are named bn.<n> (ground) and bp.<n> (5V). Rail hole numbers are approximate, taken from each wire's x position.

The button straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6. Column 4 is side 1 (1.l top, 1.r bottom) and column 6 is side 2 (2.l top, 2.r bottom). The catalogue joins 1.l with 1.r and 2.l with 2.r inside the part. Which of l/r is top or bottom is an assumption.

Orange wire: column 4 (button side 1) to the 5V rail. Teal wire: pin 2 to column 6 (button side 2). The 10k pull-down resistor runs from column 6 to column 9, and the short black wire takes column 9 to the ground rail. So pin 2 sits on the same side as the pull-down resistor, and the other side goes to 5V.
The black wire from the Arduino goes to the second GND pin on the power header, so I used GND.2. The red wire goes to 5V.
The built-in LED on pin 13 is on the board, so there is no external LED.
Parts are unchanged from step 1.

The image is the authority: the MKR Zero is not plugged into the breadboard (despite the text); it connects to the breadboard only through the three jumper wires: red to VCC (3.3 V), black to GND, orange to D7.

DHT22/RHT03 pins VCC, SDA, NC, GND go in breadboard columns 26-29, row a (top bank). The red wire shares column 26 with VCC, the orange wire column 27 with data, the black wire column 29 with GND. Column 28 (NC) is unused.
The 100nF capacitor sits between the VCC strip (column 26) and the GND strip (column 29). The 4.7k pull-up resistor sits between the VCC strip (column 26) and the data strip (column 27).

The LiPo battery connects through its JST connector to the board's battery socket; the battery's + and - leads share the single BAT port. The microSD card sits in the board's SD slot and has no ports of its own.
Everything is powered from 3.3 V (VCC), within the DHT22's 3.3-6 V range. No LED is used, so no series resistor is needed.

The E6 check is probably a false positive, so I kept every part. The graph has exactly two parts of type `resistor`: r1 (10k ohm) and r2 (220 ohm). These match the tutorial's parts list ('10k ohm resistor', '220 ohm resistor'), its circuit text and the schematic labels. There is no third resistor to remove.

The check most likely counts the photoresistor (ldr1, type `photoresistor`) as a resistor. The tutorial lists it separately as the analog sensor ('analog sensor (a photoresistor will do)'), and the image and schematic both show it. Removing it would leave the A0 divider without its sensor, so I kept it.
Circuit: 5V -> photoresistor -> junction (A0) -> 10k resistor -> GND. Pin 9 -> LED -> 220 ohm resistor -> GND.

In the breadboard image the LED's bent (longer) leg is in column 22, where the blue pin-9 wire ends. The 220 ohm resistor sits between the LED's other leg (column 23) and the ground wire in column 26. So the resistor is on the cathode side, whereas the schematic draws it on the anode side. Both are a series connection, and I followed the image.

The image labels the top half rows j-f, but the catalogue names the top half bank 't' with rows a-e. I used 't' holes and mapped the rows as j=a, i=b, h=c, g=d, f=e. Only the column strip matters electrically.
Rail hole numbers (tp.1, tp.5, tn.3, tn.10, tn.22) are estimated from the picture. Only which rail each wire uses matters.
The tutorial text says 'Analog input 2', but the circuit and schematic use A0, so I used A0.
